I don't do reviews often, infact, I don't do them at all. However WARDOGS will be my exception, as I don't feel people have been fair, to review bomb a game for a day one launch not going perfectly, or reviewing negatively because streamers got prio (Firstly who cares? This stuff happens all the time, it's healthy for smaller dev companies to do!), I'm here to review the game.

Day 1: I sat in the queue, I gave up
Day 2: I got straight in, and played the game I expected to play, a full match with 0 hiccups.

The game has run smoothly, I've had 0 crashes, 0 latency issues, 0 problems and a lot of fun. The community has been fun to jive with and I'll continue to play.

Thanks Devs!

The game is great and has a solid player base, but the biggest problem is cheaters. It’s ridiculous that someone can reach level 200 and still run around in matches without getting banned. 90% of Chinese names are cheating. If you want the end-of-match bonus, you’re left with no choice but to stay AFK somewhere until the game ends or aimlessly drive logistics for money. I hope the developers wake up quickly and fix this issue, otherwise the game will be dead within a few months.

Season 2 update: Balance is still pretty awful. New AA vehicle makes air logistics even more insufferable. There was no wipe for those that abused the Driver XP exploit to unlock tanks early.

Despite some major balancing issues at Early Access launch, the game is very fun and hilarious when it can be, and I think it has a great foundation to be a great game.

However, I have to give a negative review due to Bulkhead's CEO: Joe Brammer. It appears he's wanting to keep the "bro-culture" of game development alive and isn't shying away from having crunch happen within his studio, to the point of saying anyone decrying crunch "you're not going to be happy here, so we're not going to go with you." (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/wardogs-lead-says-the-studio-won-t-hire-people-who-decry-crunch-on-social-media?utm_source=dlvr.it&utm_medium=bluesky).

Crunch isn't a "necessary evil" in game development, it's a product of poor management skills.

As someone with multiple friends in game development from AAA to indie, this is one of the main reasons this industry is going downhill and is so toxic to any junior wanting to work in game development.

As Bulkhead's own website states on it's front page: "Be the change you want to see."

The performance and graphics are really abysmal. I should not have to use DLSS and Nvidia Reflex to get a consistent 100 FPS on medium settings with an RTX 4090. The movement and menus are clunky and cumbersome, and the loot economy (e.g., must purchase parachutes or be forced to die when helicopter pilot bails out 100 feet in the air) need a lot of rethinking. IMHO, the gameplay seems to combine the more frustrating aspects of Battlefield 6, PUBG, and Tarkov. I cannot reiterate just how lethargic and cumbersome the input is. Even if you wrestle with the graphics and achieve a reasonable framerate and tolerable visuals, the ADS speed, input lag, and player movement makes you feel like you're wearing drunk goggles. Furthermore, the visuals are very unimpressive. What is impressive is how they managed to make a game look worse AND perform worse than Arma 3, which was released 2013. I played Arma 3 in 2015 with a R9 Fury X (google it- worse than a GTX 980) and had a more visually pleasing and performant experience than this. I may check it out again in a few years, but this game has a LONG way to to, and I'll be giving it a pass.

There is literally something for everybody in this game. Run supplies, build bases, intense ground combat, air combat, lobbing artillery or mortars for big booms, etc. Tired of one playstyle? Just do something else and you still see the impact you have on your team and your own profit. One of the best modern live service shooters on the market HANDS DOWN. Do yourself a favor, spend the initial $40, and then use the extra $40 you would've used on $80 COD and buy it for your friend.

A fantastic and unique FPS that genuinely strives to give the player the freedom to participate in each game however they like. Skill demons and Bob the Builders both have their place in this game, as does the Heli pilots, the logistics drivers and the average Joe like myself.

You are not confined by loadouts, classes, perks or abilities. You want to take a sniper with defibrillators and be Combat Medic Sniper elite? go ahead. You want to listen to a podcast in the background and spend the game taxiing your team to the OBJ, go right ahead!

Wardogs feels like one the very few fps games designed from the bottom-up to be about fun and freedom. Sure does that lead to some issues in things such as balancing? Yes, but the Devs are keenly aware of this and the EA status of the game reflects that.

I truly believe Wardogs has the potential to be a genre-defining Game. Worth a try, even just once!

What is this game all about?
A sandbox FPS with a twist of arcadey milsim that is fun when you have a squad of friends. Build FOBs, infiltrate enemy FOBs, gunfights and what have you.

Current issue as of version 0.1.2
- Unable to squad up before joining a match.
- Cheaters using ESPs, aimbot etc.
- Griefers sabotaging own team mates.
- High tier balance - Guns unlocked at later stages are too OP.
- Tier 4 armor too OP. Getting a balance pass.
- Infrared Range Finder used to spot enemies too OP. Getting fixed.

Fun stuff
- Earn cash and carry forward to your next game.
- Build stuff to earn cash.
- Kill enemies to earn cash.
- Destroy enemy vehicles to earn cash.
- Destroy enemy FOBs to earn cash.
- Spot enemies to earn cash.
- Do supply delivery via land or air to earn cash.
- Cash cash cash cash cash.

If you have friends to play this with, it's a nice game. If you intend to play solo, good luck.

While the core gameplay and foundation are fantastic, the progression system needs serious balancing. The gear grind is overwhelming, and the power gap between equipment tiers (armor and weapons) is far too wide. Anyone who has level 3 and level 4 armor and weapons will one shot level 1 gear player, while level 1 player needs multiple headshot. Kill is basically only possible if it's a complete surprise attack.That's just combat... there's also tons of utility grind for medical equipment, grenades, support etc... Low level servers are a good addition on paper, but only if you plan to play solo, if you are playing with friends you can't really use them if anyone is over level 50. Wipe on 15th will improve this for a while but if the balancing remains similar I see this as a major hurdle for new players.

I've played alot of FPS shooters, this game is nothing like any other game. I have earnings playing valorant, still never have had this fun on a game in a long ass time. The shit talk is actually funny, gunplay is balanced, devs actually care about their game. First review ive made because its worth it.

It was great fun for about the first week of early access, and then the unemployed masses unlocked the ridiculously over powered end game equipment. Now, you will be spotted 24/7 by thermal recon players, and then beamed across the map by M4s ripping in full auto from players in full T4 armor that is nearly impossible to defeat with standard ammunition. All this is to say, the gap in effectiveness between the highest level gear, and the gear just prior to it, is exponential. And, unless you have countless hours to invest in to the game in a short period of time, you will NOT have a good time if you want to experience the infantry combat side of the game. I will revisit this review if/when season 2 improves the meta. But right now, it is simply not enjoyable any more.

One major issue sucks the fun out of an otherwise enjoyable game: the progression system.

The worst example of this is the armor progression. Level 3 body armor is locked behind 50+ hours of grinding, and once you get it you become basically invincible to all the plebs. The counter for strong armor, AP rounds, is locked behind another 50+ hour grind on top of that.

You need to play this game like a full time job just grinding in order to keep up with unlocks. If you fall behind, you will no longer face fair fights. Your peashooter guns will do nothing against a no-life chad, and you will constantly get stomped into the dirt even if you get the drop on someone.

The amount of grinding needed to get to endgame unlocks is also completely ridiculous. I feel like I'm playing Runescape here trying to get 99 in a skill. Except in Wardogs, progression is planned to wipe regularly, so have fun grinding 100+ hours to get to max level for each skill tree every few months when the wipe happens.

If you want to play this casually or have better things to do than grind Wardogs 8 hours a day, do not bother playing this.

War Dogs starts out almost charming — a solid three-hour honeymoon period where you can almost convince yourself the developers had a pulse. Then the lobbies fill up with the exact same mid-tier CS rejects who peaked in 2019, and the illusion dies screaming.
There’s no anti-cheat. Reports do nothing. The AK is less a weapon and more a ceremonial ladle for stirring the steaming, unfiltered shit-pot this game has become. The core idea isn’t even terrible, which somehow makes it worse. Shipping a multiplayer shooter in 2025 without anti-cheat is the digital equivalent of pissing directly into the wind, then turning around with a straight face and declaring “actually, this is kind of refreshing.”
It’s not rocket science. YouTube is already a highlight reel of cheaters demonstrating what the “average” match looks like for the rest of us peasants. I should never have bought this. I didn’t just waste money — I got mugged at point-blank range by a game that looked me dead in the eye and whispered “trust me, bro.”

Great game, this can easily become a household name for milsim games. Many of the mechanics and roles are in really good spots and lets you contribute in a lot of ways from transport, logistics, construction, artillery, infantry, scouting, etc. And for how large scale matches are, it's surprisingly well optimized. One of the most fun shooters I've played in a very long time.

The one issue is that this game is very much focused on vertical progression, so it's extremely favored to people who have sunk more time into the game. People with Tier 3 and 4 armour are very clearly advantaged despite the weight penalties. And it can be difficult to deal with it because the counterplay (armor piercing rounds) are unlocked pretty late into progression.

Season 2 ruined the game!

First things first, I want to say that it was REALLY FUN to play during Season 1, even with small bugs, BLUE TEAM and even unbalanced weapons.

But Season 2 absolutely destroyed everything! T-72 a few hours after the servers started, exploits and fast XP gain made this game a nightmare even for those who spent a lot of time in Wardogs, not to mention the average Wardogs player.

Another story is the HUGE nerf of the scout AKA sniper role. DMRs are completely useless after the balance changes. Imagine 3 weapons (SVD, BMR and M14) having the same damage. You have to land 4 shots in a row to get a kill!

I don't know how they could have fucked up after getting so much attention from the gaming community and selling 3M copies. Shame on you, devs!
